questions.question: In imperial China, traditional woodblock printed books were folded and stitched at the side as an 'accordion book' because:
options: Chinese calligraphy characters could only be read horizontally
The porous and thin paper could not be printed on both sides
Emperors ordered that all books must look like musical instruments
Glue was legally prohibited in Chinese publishing
questions.explanation: Because traditional Chinese paper was thin and porous, ink seeped through, making two-sided printing impossible; therefore sheets were folded and bound as accordion books.

questions.question: Why did wealthy European aristocrats in fifteenth-century Europe initially scoff at printed books and refuse to keep them in their personal libraries?
options: Printed books were printed only in Latin which aristocrats did not understand
The Church threatened to excommunicate anyone owning a printed book
Gutenberg refused to sell books to aristocrats

questions.explanation: Wealthy aristocrats regarded printed volumes as crude and vulgar copies meant for commoners, treasuring handwritten manuscripts on luxurious animal vellum as true marks of prestige.

questions.question: How did Johann Gutenberg's upbringing and craft skills enable him to invent movable metal type?

He worked in a paper manufacturing factory in Venice

questions.question: How did early printers bridge the cultural gap between the small literate minority and the vast illiterate majority in early modern Europe?
options: By offering free university evening classes to all peasants
By printing popular ballads, folk tales, and religious texts illustrated with pictures that were recited and sung aloud in village taverns and gatherings
By producing books with audio recordings
By printing books only in sign language
questions.explanation: Because most common people could not read, publishers printed illustrated ballads and folktales that could be sung or recited aloud in communal taverns, seamlessly blending oral culture with print.

questions.question: Why did the Latin scholar and Catholic reformer Erasmus express deep anxiety about the flood of printed books in his 1508 work 'Adages'?
options: He wanted all printing presses to be converted into paper recycling mills
He believed books made human beings physically blind
He feared that uncontrolled printing filled the world with ignorant, scandalous, irreligious, and seditious books that degraded scholarly value
He feared that Latin would be replaced by Chinese
questions.explanation: Erasmus worried that the unrestrained proliferation of printing flooded the world with swarms of worthless, defamatory, and heretical books that drowned out true scholarly and religious wisdom.

questions.explanation: Enlightenment thinkers' writings were printed widely in pocketbooks and pamphlets, enabling ordinary readers to judge royal authority, church dogma, and tradition through the prism of reason.

questions.question: When the Grimm Brothers in Germany collected traditional folk tales from peasants, what editorial changes did they make before publishing them in 1812?

They converted every human character into an animal
